findings.claim: The commit says the landing rule names no branch, and the new test comment at engine/skills/inception_family_artifact_test.go:129 says 'The landing rule names no branch: neither the default one nor a selected one.' The landing anchor section still says 'more than one commit on the default branch carries it' (line 40). The landing definition (lines 30-31) no longer names a branch, but the ambiguity check is still limited to the default branch. A change that lands on a non-default tracker or integration branch would be checked against the wrong branch. The new pin cannot catch this: rejectClauses only rejects 'onto the default branch', and line 40 says 'on the default branch'. Line 40 itself is unchanged and was already inconsistent with the earlier 'selected integration branch' wording. The new comment and commit message now state an invariant that the file does not meet.

For a non-terminal chain, or an error because the chain has no records, the instruction changed from 'means it still runs: wait' to 'means it runs: do not fire'. The new wording no longer tells the parent to wait and check again. It only forbids firing closure, so a reader could drop closure for that change instead of putting it off. The terminal-but-unlanded case still says 'wait for landing'. The changed requireClauses pin fixes the new wording in place.
